todoContent: Understand all product contracts (CEM, RH, RMD_H, RMD_X, MCP2515 CAN)
functionalSummary: Read all motor protocol contracts (CEM, RH, RMD_H, RMD_X) and CAN bus specifications (MCP2515), and explored the existing ESP32 firmware architecture including driver implementations and protocol layers.
detailSummary: This work established foundational understanding of the motor control system architecture. Six contract documents were read covering CAN protocol specifications, ESP32 firmware requirements, and four motor types (CEM, RH, RMD_H, RMD_X). The existing firmware structure was explored, revealing a layered architecture: hardware drivers (MCP2515 CAN, RS485) → CAN bus abstraction (can_bus) → protocol abstraction layer (pal) → motor-specific drivers (cem_driver, rh_driver, rmd_x_driver). Configuration is centralized in config.h and constants.h using #define macros. The Logger class provides static logging with configurable levels. This exploration identified the code organization pattern that future implementation work should follow: new motor support requires adding a driver in src/drivers/, integrating with the CAN bus abstraction, and potentially extending the protocol layer.
keyPatterns: Driver structure: Each motor type (cem, rh, rmd_x) has separate driver files (driver.h/cpp) in firmware/esp32/src/drivers/
CAN bus abstraction: can_bus.h/cpp wraps MCP2515 hardware driver (mcp2515_can.h/cpp) for protocol-agnostic CAN communication
Protocol layer: pal.cpp/h implements protocol abstraction layer on top of CAN bus drivers
Configuration: config.h uses #define macros for pin mappings and constants; constants.h for protocol-specific values
Logging: Logger class with static methods (_level, _timestamp) and LOG_LEVEL_* constants
Types: types.h defines custom types and enums used across the firmware
